meta.what: A1: every euro that reached Ukraine 24 Jan 2022 - 31 Aug 2026 (bilateral aid incl. in-kind, EU institutions incl. EIB, G7 ERA loans, IMF/World Bank/EBRD/CEB own-risk money, private donations, undisclosed military aid, Ukraine's own budget spent on arms abroad), each euro assigned once to (a) what it paid for and (b) the economy where it was spent (seller). A2: purchases donors made to replace weapons they gave, only where explicitly a replacement, capped at donated value, by buyer, seller and year.
meta.units: EUR bn gross (revenue, not profit), nominal; years 2022-2025 calendar, 2026 = Jan-Aug (not annualised). USD at ECB yearly averages 2022 1.053, 2023 1.081, 2024 1.082, 2025 1.13, 2026 1.16. Kiel values in EUR as given; Kiel's few pre-2022 months folded into 2022.
meta.method: Row by row over Kiel's 5,587 allocation rows (EUR 382.9bn) plus non-Kiel lines. Military: coded procurement location -> that seller; PURL and JUMPSTART -> USA; Czech initiative -> origin split; own stocks -> 'stock' (no new spending; replacement in A2); unlocated procurement -> donor's domestic share pu (flowback2), then Ukrainian producers (Kiel trend 2-25%), then a foreign pattern (50% Kiel-coded third-country purchases, 50% EU/EEA arms production); unknown-source rows split by the donor's coded stock share. US unlocated procurement 88% USA / 4% Ukraine / 8% abroad (CSIS). Financial: budget support -> Ukraine (pensions/social 60%, public salaries 37%, other 3%, Ukrainian MoF); energy-tagged -> energy equipment basket; EU UIF/IFI guarantees -> guaranteed investment (70% Ukraine); EIB -> infrastructure (60% Ukraine); swap line -> not spent. Humanitarian: UN/NGO cash 60% Ukraine; in-kind 85% donor economy; energy aid -> energy basket. Ranges: each entry carries a certainty letter with factors A 0.9-1.1, B 0.8-1.25, C 0.6-1.5, D 0.35-2.0; seller low/high sum these (fully correlated, wide).

fields.countries.<ISO3>.new_spending_eur_bn: money actually spent in that economy for Ukraine, by year, low/central/high (excludes donated own stocks)
fields.by_source_and_type: keys '<source>|<type>'; source = own_aid (seller's own government aid), other_donors (other governments' bilateral aid), EU (Commission/Council/EIB, excl. ERA), ERA (G7 ERA loans incl. EU's), multilateral (IMF, World Bank own-risk, EBRD, CEB), UKR_budget (Ukraine's own budget), private; type = weapons / other
fields.memo_own_stock_donations_kiel_value: Kiel value of the seller's own-stock donations: not money spent in 2022-26; replacement spending is in replacement_* fields
fields.replacement_sales_eur_bn: A2: replacement purchases (by any buyer) paid to this seller, by year of payment, low/central/high
fields.replacement_bought_by_seller_total: A2: this country as BUYER of replacements, by seller
fields.already_in_customs_trade_eur_bn: from ua_arms_purchases: part of this seller's arms sales to Ukraine that customs data (and so sell_ukr) already records
fields.compare_existing_flowback_central_2022_2: existing site/data.json flowback fields vs the ledger fields that replace them

meta.how_to_use: REPLACE, do not add. For each seller: (1) flowback.own -> by_source_and_type['own_aid|weapons'] + replacement bought from itself (replacement_bought_by_seller_total[ISO3]); (2) flowback.purl_in -> for USA: part of 'other_donors|weapons' (PURL 5.5, JUMPSTART 1.1, Kiel-coded donor purchases in the US incl. German Patriots 3.2, Norway, Canada); for EU members: 'EU|weapons'; (3) flowback.arms -> 'other_donors|weapons' + 'UKR_budget|weapons' + 'ERA|weapons' (+ 'private|weapons'), minus already_in_customs_trade_eur_bn as before; (4) replacement purchases from OTHER countries (replacement_sales minus the seller's own replacement buying) are new war-effort earnings for that seller; (5) 'other' type (budget support, energy, humanitarian, reconstruction spent in donor and third economies) is new; its use is the builder's choice (A5). Ukraine (UKR) is the recipient, not an earner. _UNALLOC is money spent abroad with no known seller.

overlaps: This ledger is a re-cut of money already counted on the GIVING side (Kiel aid in kiel.json, loans_value, weapons_value, uncovered.json private/undisclosed) - those stay as they are; the ledger only says WHERE the money was spent. On the EARNING side it supersedes, for each seller: flowback.own (flowback.json / flowback2 own_industry shares), flowback.purl_in (USA PURL from flowback.json; EU members' EU-level arms slice), and flowback.arms (ua_arms_purchases add_to_map_gross). Main differences: (a) own stocks no longer count as own-industry spending through r (flowback2 'own_stocks x r'); restocking enters only through A2 where explicit and paid by Aug 2026 (e.g. GBR, ITA, NLD fall); (b) USA: CSIS-style 0.88 x military aid (EUR 56.9bn) is replaced by USAI-type procurement 29.9 + replenishment paid 20.7 (A2) + allied purchases 16.0 + Ukraine-paid FMS; (c) ua_arms add_to_map netted customs trade; the ledger is gross, so subtract already_in_customs_trade_eur_bn (POL, SVK, ROU mainly) to stay consistent with sell_ukr; (d) Czech sales are pinned to the Czech licence totals (MIT) via a residual paid by Ukraine; (e) Ukraine's own foreign purchases (UKR_budget, EUR 14.6bn) are paid from a budget that budget support also funds - money is fungible, so donors' budget support is assigned to Ukraine (first round) and the foreign arms bill to 'UKR_budget', never both. Refugee costs are not money reaching Ukraine and are not in the ledger. EPF reimbursements (EU to member states for donated stocks) are transfers between donors, not to Ukraine: memo only. Not double counted: the Kiel-coded 'procured in Czechia' rows (DNK 1.33, NLD 0.41) and the initiative are inside the CZE licence total.
notes: Allocation timing: Kiel allocations (contracted/delivered) are used as the year of spending, as in the rest of the map; USAI deliveries were only 57.3% of appropriations by Aug 2026 (CRS), so US spending is front-loaded relative to cash flows.

Guarantees (EUR 22.5bn) are counted at face value as money that reached Ukraine via the IFIs that lent against them (WB ADVANCE, UK WB guarantees as budget support; EU UIF as investment). The IFIs' own-risk lending is separate (multilateral) and excludes guaranteed volumes.
Multilateral money is gross disbursement; Ukraine also repaid IMF ~USD 2-3bn a year (memo, not netted).

A2 values are payments made by Aug 2026 (estimated from contract values and delivery schedules); contracted-but-unpaid replacement value is larger (e.g. German and Romanian Patriots, Finnish authorities to 2028).
A2 USA: replenishment appropriations (USD 39.3bn, DoD IG) exceed the USD 31.8bn of items given; capped at 31.8bn, 50-80% paid by Aug 2026.
No explicit replacement purchases were found for ITA, ESP, BEL, CAN, LTU, LVA, PRT, AUS (searched); they get 0 replacement and lose the r-based stock refill in flowback2.
